import itertools
from pysat import CNF, Solver

n = 14
fixed_edges = [(1,11), (0,13), (7,9), (1,13), (4,11), (6,9)]

# All possible edges (undirected, u < v)
all_edges = [(i,j) for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n)]

# Map each edge to a SAT variable
edge_to_var = {e: idx+1 for idx, e in enumerate(all_edges)}
var_to_edge = {idx+1: e for idx, e in enumerate(all_edges)}

cnf = CNF()

# Fixed edges must be present
for e in fixed_edges:
    cnf.add_clause([edge_to_var[e]])

# For each vertex, degree must be 4 or 5
# We can encode: degree >= 4 AND degree <= 5
# degree >= 4: at least 4 of the incident edges are true
# degree <= 5: at most 5 of the incident edges are true

# For each vertex, get incident edges
incident = {v: [] for v in range(n)}
for e in all_edges:
    i,j = e
    incident[i].append(e)
    incident[j].append(e)

# At most 5: for each vertex, no 6 edges can be simultaneously true
# So for each combination of 6 incident edges, at least one must be false
for v in range(n):
    edges_v = incident[v]
    # At most 5: for any 6 edges, not all can be true
    for combo in itertools.combinations(edges_v, 6):
        cnf.add_clause([-edge_to_var[e] for e in combo])
    
    # At least 4: for any (len-3) edges, not all can be false
    # i.e., for any set of (len-3) edges, at least one must be true
    # Actually, degree >= 4 means we cannot have (len-4) edges all false
    # So for any combination of (len-4) edges, not all can be false
    # Which means: for any set of (len-4) edges, at least one is true
    k = len(edges_v) - 4
    if k > 0:
        for combo in itertools.combinations(edges_v, k):
            cnf.add_clause([edge_to_var[e] for e in combo])

print(f"Variables: {len(all_edges)}, Clauses: {len(cnf.clauses)}")

solver = Solver(bootstrap_with=cnf)
if solver.solve():
    model = solver.get_model()
    solution_edges = [var_to_edge[abs(v)] for v in model if v > 0]
    print(f"Solution found with {len(solution_edges)} edges")
    print("Edges:", sorted(solution_edges))
    
    # Verify degrees
    deg = [0]*n
    for u,v in solution_edges:
        deg[u] += 1
        deg[v] += 1
    print("Degrees:", deg)
    print("All between 4 and 5?", all(4 <= d <= 5 for d in deg))
else:
    print("UNSATISFIABLE")
